explanation: The ECU sealed the fuel vapor system and watched for pressure decay, and found a small leak. A small EVAP leak is most often the gas cap or a cracked hose — not an expensive part. The EVAP monitor only runs under specific conditions, so verification takes several drive cycles.

repairs.label: Replace gas cap
repairs.verification: Clear the code and drive normally for 3+ drive cycles — the EVAP monitor only runs under specific conditions (varied fuel level, cold start). If P0442 does not return, the cap was the cause.

repairs.label: Replace damaged EVAP hose section / canister
repairs.verification: Clear the code; the EVAP monitor needs several drive cycles with varied fuel level to run to completion. Confirm it runs and passes.

repairs.label: Replace EVAP vent / purge valve
repairs.verification: Clear the code and complete 3+ drive cycles; confirm the EVAP monitor runs and passes.

safety.stop_message: Raw fuel smell or a visible fuel leak: do not drive — this is a fire risk. Seek professional service.

tests.question: Remove the gas cap. Is the seal cracked, flattened, dry-rotted, or missing — or does the cap fail to click when tightened?
Under the vehicle near the fuel tank and charcoal canister: any cracked, rotted, or disconnected EVAP hoses, damaged canister, or loose fittings?
A shop smoke test was performed on the EVAP system. Did smoke escape from the vent / purge valve assembly?

title: Evaporative emission system leak detected (small leak)
